title: benchmarks.py run pool runs a whole record in one command under one spend cap
goal: python3 _tools/benchmarks.py run pool takes per-arm reps and kinds (--arm-reps ARM=N, --arm-kinds ARM=K+K, the default for an arm not named being --reps and --kinds), both shapes in one run (--shape fresh,session) and a stratified subset (--sample N: N rows per kind, seeded), so a record such as 2026-10-08's (kb arms at 3 reps, Sonnet 5.5 at 2, web arms on six kinds, the session shape) is one invocation with one --max-usd over all of it, one set of spend rows and one log; --dry-run prints the plan per arm label and the spend estimate; a test plans such a record with a fake runner and checks the runs per label, --sample's rows and the cap across both shapes; kb/_self/tools.md and the pool section name the flags

gates.question: How does --sample N pick its rows?
options: N rows of each kind, drawn per kind by a generator seeded from --seed and the kind, over the whole pool before any kind filter; the kept rows keep the pool's order
N rows of each kind, drawn after --kinds and --arm-kinds, so an arm's sample depends on its kinds
gates.recommendation: N rows of each kind, drawn per kind by a generator seeded from --seed and the kind, over the whole pool before any kind filter; the kept rows keep the pool's order
gates.answer: N rows of each kind, drawn per kind by a generator seeded from --seed and the kind, over the whole pool before any kind filter; the kept rows keep the pool's order

gates.question: What does the session shape do with --arm-kinds and --arm-reps?
options: A key ARM applies to both shapes, a key ARM/session overrides it in the session shape only, and each session arm's groups are built from its own kinds
Only ARM keys exist and they apply to both shapes; the session shape groups the same rows for every arm
The session shape ignores both flags and takes --kinds and --reps
gates.recommendation: A key ARM applies to both shapes, a key ARM/session overrides it in the session shape only, and each session arm's groups are built from its own kinds
gates.answer: A key ARM applies to both shapes, a key ARM/session overrides it in the session shape only, and each session arm's groups are built from its own kinds

gates.question: How is the one --max-usd shared between the shapes of a run, and what does a stop exit with?
options: The shapes run in the order given; each starts runs only while the spend of the whole run so far is under the cap, so a shape after a spent cap starts none and records every unit as spend_stopped; exit 1 as with one shape
The cap is split between the shapes by their estimated spend
The cap applies to the first shape only
gates.recommendation: The shapes run in the order given; each starts runs only while the spend of the whole run so far is under the cap, so a shape after a spent cap starts none and records every unit as spend_stopped; exit 1 as with one shape
gates.answer: within a shape the labels' runs start one of each in turn, and the cap is shared between the shapes by their estimated spend over what is left; a stop exits 1 (changed in the review: BG-kwxzwsfd implements it, its gate g3)

gates.question: What is the syntax of --shape, --arm-reps and --arm-kinds, and how are bad values handled?
options: --shape takes fresh, session or both comma separated; --arm-reps and --arm-kinds take ARM=VALUE pairs comma separated or by repeating the flag, kinds joined by +; an unknown shape, arm or kind, a repeated key, or an arm the run does not run (opus-5-5 without --arms, a session key without the session shape) exits 2 with a message, and --kinds is checked against the known kinds too
The same syntax, but a name the run does not run is a warning and is ignored
gates.recommendation: --shape takes fresh, session or both comma separated; --arm-reps and --arm-kinds take ARM=VALUE pairs comma separated or by repeating the flag, kinds joined by +; an unknown shape, arm or kind, a repeated key, or an arm the run does not run (opus-5-5 without --arms, a session key without the session shape) exits 2 with a message, and --kinds is checked against the known kinds too
gates.answer: --shape takes fresh, session or both comma separated; --arm-reps and --arm-kinds take ARM=VALUE pairs comma separated or by repeating the flag, kinds joined by +; an unknown shape, arm or kind, a repeated key, or an arm the run does not run (opus-5-5 without --arms, a session key without the session shape) exits 2 with a message, and --kinds is checked against the known kinds too

gates.question: With --shape fresh,session and --arms, which arms does each shape run?
options: fresh runs the arms named (default DEFAULT_ARMS); session runs those of them that are session arms, else all session arms; an arm named that no shape can run is an error only under --shape session alone
Both shapes run the arms named, and a non-session arm in the session shape is an error
gates.recommendation: fresh runs the arms named (default DEFAULT_ARMS); session runs those of them that are session arms, else all session arms; an arm named that no shape can run is an error only under --shape session alone
gates.answer: fresh runs the arms named (default DEFAULT_ARMS); session runs those of them that are session arms, else all session arms; an arm named that no shape can run is an error only under --shape session alone
